archetype.name: Play-In Exit (unlucky at the margins)
archetype.definition: A faster, more balanced Heat played like a solid mid-pack team over 82 games, but a poor record in close games left it in the play-in, and it went out there.

report.headline: A faster, better Heat that close games and the play-in sent home

recap.finish: 43-39, fourth in the Southeast; lost in the play-in
recap.body:
This was a different-looking Miami team. For years the Heat played slowly and won with defense. This one ran at a Pace of 103.4 against a league average of 99.4, well above anything in its recent history, which sat around 96. That tempo inflates the raw numbers. Its 120.87 points a game ranked 2nd and its 118.54 allowed ranked 22nd, but per possession it was simply good on both ends: 116.7 ORtg and 114.5 DRtg, both 13th, for a Net Rtg of 2.2. The offense was the improved side, up from 21st in each of the last two years. The defense slid from the top-ten group it had been every year since 2020-21.

The season peaked early. A 10-5 November had the Heat at 13-7, and the 7-game winning streak came in that stretch. December went 5-8 and January 8-9, which dropped them to 26-24. From then on they were a .500 team. February was the best defensive month of the year at 110.64 allowed a game, and it still only produced a 6-5 record. March went 8-7 and April 3-3.

The gap between the margin and the record is the real story. A +191 point differential implies 47 wins. The Heat won 43, and their W vs Pt Diff of -4 ranked 27th. With ATL taking the division at 46-36, a few close games breaking the other way would have meant a playoff seed instead of the play-in. It wasn't a one-year fluke either: last year's 37-45 team carried a -5 on the same measure.

The frontcourt carried the team and earned an A- grade. Bam Adebayo led in minutes (2365), points (1468) and Win Shares (6.4), made All-Defensive Second Team, and posted a team-best +9.5 On-Off. Kel'el Ware added 6.2 Win Shares on 61.6 TS %. Norman Powell, an All-Star, scored 1261 points on 60.9 TS % in 58 games, though the team was 3.6 points worse with him on the floor. The ball security was elite, with a TOV % of 11.6 ranking 4th.

The end was shaky. Over the last ten games the Heat went 5-5 while allowing 126.2 a game, 7.66 worse than their season average. They lost twice in Toronto and gave up 147 to Boston and 149 to Cleveland before closing with two blowout wins. A defense leaking that badly is a hard thing to take into a one-game elimination, and the season ended in the play-in.

highlights.title: Adebayo and Ware anchor the frontcourt
highlights.body: The two centers produced the most Win Shares on the roster and drove an A- frontcourt grade. Adebayo's +9.5 On-Off was the clearest individual signal on the team. Ware was efficient and productive in fewer minutes, so this group is the most reliable base for next year.

highlights.title: An offense that finally climbed
highlights.body: After two years ranked 21st, the offense moved up to 13th in offensive rating. Speeding up helped, and so did elite turnover avoidance: the Heat wasted fewer possessions than all but three teams. It is a skill-based gain rather than a shooting spike, since its eFG % was slightly below the league average.

highlights.title: Better than its record
highlights.body: The point differential implies a 47-win team, not a 43-win one. That margin ranked 13th per game, which is real mid-table quality. The record undersold how well the Heat actually played.

lowlights.title: Close games cost a playoff seed
lowlights.body: A W vs Pt Diff of -4 ranked 27th, and in a division decided by a few games that was the difference between a seed and the play-in. Close-game results usually even out. Still, two straight years on the wrong side, after -5 last season, is worth watching.

lowlights.title: Defense slipped, and collapsed late
lowlights.body: The defense fell to 13th after years in the top ten. Point guards hurt it most: opponents' PGs piled up more combined points, rebounds and assists against Miami than against any other team. Over the final ten games it allowed 126.2 a game, far worse than its season level, just as the play-in arrived.

lowlights.title: Jović's year was a drain
lowlights.body: The one power forward in the rotation shot 48 TS % with a -3.5 BPM and produced no Win Shares in 808 minutes. That is a weak spot in an otherwise strong frontcourt, and the fourth frontcourt spot needs to be fixed or replaced.

arc.note: A 13-7 start built on a 10-5 November gave way to a December slide and a .500 team from January on, ending with a leaky last ten games.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is the Adebayo-Ware frontcourt, plus an offense that climbed into the middle of the league by protecting the ball. The margin says this roster is a high-40s-win team, so some of the gap to 43 wins should close on its own if close games even out. That said, two straight years of underperforming the differential is not nothing. The work is on defense and in the backcourt. The B- backcourt let opposing point guards do more against Miami than almost anywhere else. Powell's scoring came with a negative On-Off, and Mitchell's +3.3 On-Off came on low usage. The power forward spot needs more than Jović gave. Restoring the defense to its usual top-ten level is the clearest path from the play-in back to a playoff seed.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season; play-in result given only in status
